title: starter-signal-onboarding-pocket-and-access-cushion
summary: A compact, manager-facing onboarding blueprint that combines an interview rubric, a hiring-phase plan, and a 21-day "access cushion" checklist for senior and cross-functional hires. Designed for staggered, low-meeting "quiet" launches and neurodiversity/return-from-leave accommodations.
hiring_plan: Target role buckets: senior platform / infra / applied-ml ICs (2-3 hires per quarter). Timeline: 4-week candidate velocity target (screen -> take-home -> onsite-lite -> offer). Owner: people-ops recruiter + hiring manager. Acceptance driver: clear path to first deliverable + 1:1 alignment with manager within first week. Benchmarks: offer acceptance rate >= 65% for prioritized candidates; time-to-offer median <= 21 days.
interview_rubric: Problem decomposition (scale 1-5) — looks for structured breakdown, tradeoffs, and simple measurable outcomes; 4+ preferred for senior ICs.
System design (scale 1-5) — depth of API/infra thinking, deploy considerations, failure modes, and operational cost reasoning.
Code craft (scale 1-5) — clarity, testability, and pragmatic tradeoffs rather than perfect implementation; accept a strong design with lightweight code for senior roles.
Collaboration signals (scale 1-5) — cross-team communication, stakeholder alignment examples, asynchronous collaboration practices.
On-call & reliability experience (scale 1-5) — incident postmortem depth, runbook familiarity, tooling exposure.
Bias mitigation notes — use structured questions, blind score sheets for take-homes, and require justification when scores deviate >2 points between interviewers.
Red flags — inability to describe prior ownership, dismissive of operational constraints, repeated score of 1 in collaboration or reliability.
Hiring decision rule — hire when median >=4 and no score <2; exceptions require hiring manager + recruiter + 1 peer consensus documented in comment thread.
21_day_onboarding_checklist: Pre-boarding (week before start): hardware order + access tickets open; short 'welcome packet' email with org map + buddy intro; calendar hold for quiet-first-week (max 3 hours/day).
Day 0: account access verification, security walkthrough (30m), buddy intro async doc; manager sends 3-thing-first-week expectations email.
Day 1-3: low-density schedule — two short syncs (30m) maximum per day, deep-works blocks reserved; run local dev + read README doc; pair with buddy for repo tour (1h).
End of week 1: milestone 1 — merge a trivial but real PR (doc fix / small config change) and short retro with manager (30m).
Week 2: ramp tasks — first feature scaffold assigned with clear acceptance criteria; weekly 1:1 established; invite to recurring team rituals but optional; feedback loop for meeting density.
Week 3: deliverable checkpoint — demo scoped work, identify blockers, 1:1 alignment on next 30 days; ramp buddy to hand off day-to-day ops tasks.
Ongoing: schedule a 30/60/90 sync cadence between manager and new hire; people-ops triage check at day 14 to capture accommodation needs and satisfaction signals.
accommodation_guidelines: Principles: reduce cognitive load early, provide asynchronous alternatives, and create an 'access cushion' (extra time, optional meetings, clear written context). Examples: allow late start for first two weeks (start-of-day window), provide recordings and written notes for every meeting, protect two 90-minute deep work blocks per day, and assign a visible buddy for 30 days. For neurodivergent hires or people returning from leave: pre-approve reduced meeting schedules, flexible check-in formats (chat-first 1:1), and optional phased access to production systems with paired approvals.
manager_playbook: Before start: review the specific candidate's interview notes and highlight 2 immediate ways they will add value. During week 0-3: keep meetings short, set crystallized deliverables, and over-communicate context. At day 14: run a 'cognitive load check' — ask three questions: (1) what was unclear, (2) what took the most time, (3) what do you need from me this week? Document answers in the onboarding folder. Escalation path: if progress or fit concerns arise, open a people-ops flag within 48 hours with contextual notes.
rollout_notes: Pilot this package with hiring managers in infra and applied-ml for Q4 hires (target 6 pilots). Collect quick survey at day 14 and structured manager feedback at day 30. Success metrics: new-hire activation time (first merged PR) reduced variability, new-hire NPS (day 14) >= 7, and reduction in early attrition signals in first 90 days.
